newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hesse-No EMU for Germany if criteria not met.
newsitem.headline: Hesse-No EMU for Germany if criteria not met.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse said on Thursday that Germany would not be able to join Europe's planned monetary union should it fail to meet the criteria set down in the Maastricht Treaty.
Hesse also told reporters, after delivering a speech on monetary union, that the current developments in the dollar were merely part of normal fluctuations.
Hesse-No EMU for Germany if criteria not met=2

Hesse also said he was in favour of a strict interpretation of the Maastricht criteria. The deadline for the start of currency union was January 1 1999, he said, and the treaty did not foresee any delay.
Countries could always make another attempt to join the currency union a year later, he added.
Hesse's comments came as worries persist that Germany might not get its public finances in order to make the grade to launch the euro.
Sources at the European Commission said on Thursday that Germany's government debt would hover just above the 60 percent of GDP reference level set in the Maastricht treaty this year.
The decision on which countries qualify for monetary union will be made in early 1998 on the basis of 1997 data.
